title: The Art of War
author: Sun Tzu · Shénbǐ
description: The whole book, all 13 chapters, to read in Chinese page by page, with Lionel Giles' English translation on every page and the meaning of any word you tap. Plus its key words (将 general, 胜 victory, 知彼知己…), a war chariot, drum, banner, bow and bamboo slips for your world, and 11 sentences to read. Text: Sun Tzu (public domain); English: Lionel Giles, 1910 (public domain); word meanings: CC-CEDICT (CC BY-SA 4.0), so this pack is shared under CC BY-SA 4.0 too.

words.hint: 子 here means 'master', not 'child': Master Sun (Sun Wu), a general about 2,500 years ago.

words.hint: 兵 soldiers + 法 method. The book is called 孙子兵法.
Two hands at the bottom holding an axe (斤) on top: a soldier.
In this book 将 is read jiàng and means 'the general'.
冖 a cover over 车 chariots: an army camp.
攵 (a hand holding a stick) on the right: the one you fight.
讠 speech + 十 ten: talking through every option. Chapter 1 is 始计, 'Laying Plans'.
戈 (a dagger-axe) on the right: fighting.
The most important word of the book: 'victory'.
贝 (a shell: money) + 攵 (striking): broken treasure, defeat.
工 + 攵 (striking): to attack.
宀 (a roof) over 寸 (a hand): guarding the house.

Books were written on strips of bamboo (竹) tied together; that's how 孙子兵法 was first written.
战 battle + 鼓 drum: drums told the army to advance.
Drums and banners carried the general's orders (chapter 7).
战 battle + 车 car (you know it).

sentences.en: Know the enemy and know yourself, and in a hundred battles you will never be in danger.
I am the general; you are the soldier.
The enemy is attacking; I am defending.

pages.en: Sun Tzŭ said: The art of war is of vital importance to the State. It is a matter of life and death, a road either to safety or to ruin. Hence it is a subject of inquiry which can on no account be neglected. The art of war, then, is governed by five constant factors, to be taken into account in one’s deliberations, when seeking to determine the conditions obtaining in the field.

pages.en: It is owing to his information, again, that we can cause the doomed spy to carry false tidings to the enemy. Lastly, it is by his information that the surviving spy can be used on appointed occasions. The end and aim of spying in all its five varieties is knowledge of the enemy; and this knowledge can only be derived, in the first instance, from the converted spy. Hence it is essential that the converted spy be treated with the utmost liberality.

pages.en: Of old, the rise of the Yin dynasty was due to I Chih who had served under the Hsia. Likewise, the rise of the Chou dynasty was due to Lü Ya who had served under the Yin. Hence it is only the enlightened ruler and the wise general who will use the highest intelligence of the army for purposes of spying, and thereby they achieve great results. Spies are a most important element in war, because on them depends an army’s ability to move.
